cast.name: Brad Parscale
cast.bio: Trump's 2016 digital director and 2020 campaign manager; Salem Media Group's Chief Strategy Officer since January 2025, per Salem's own announcement. Sole member of Clock Tower X, a single-member Delaware LLC formed June 11, 2025, ninety-nine days before it registered as an agent of the State of Israel. Contracted through Havas Media Germany to deliver, per the filed services agreement: 100 root creative assets and 5,000 variants per month, 50 million paid impressions monthly, SEO via the MarketBrew AI platform, and 'deployment of websites and content to deliver GPT framing results on GPT conversations.' The December 2025 agreement restructured the launch budget to a $9 million pool and added monthly 'influence and network maps'; a June 2026 order added $31.5 million for April through October. The May supplemental shows $15 million received and a $750,000 repayment of his personal loan to the company. He signs every filing on the docket. Detailed questions sent August 7, 2026, deadline August 13; no response to any inquiry in this investigation to date.

cast.name: Havas Media Germany GmbH (managing directors: Sven Traichel, Gavin Jonderko, Andreas Lutzel, Christian Gaffal, Jan Altmeyer)
cast.bio: The intermediary between the State of Israel and the American operators. Sworn in Clock Tower's exhibit as 'Supervised by: State of Israel' for this engagement. Contracts and pays Clock Tower X (the $9 million pool, then the $31.5 million order) and wired Show Faith by Works' church campaign. Files nothing in the United States itself; its US sister agency, Havas Media USA, has been separately registered since 2022 on the tourism account. The five managing directors are named on the letterhead of the June 2026 order inside a DOJ filing (Frankfurt registry HRB 57024). Professional records only; no individual conduct asserted.

cast.name: Guy Getz
cast.role: Head of Advertising, LAPAM (Israel's Government Advertising Agency)
cast.bio: The connective signature across the whole pipeline, 2023 to 2026: named government-side official on Havas USA's 2023 tourism exhibit, on TCG's re-papering under the tourism pipe, and recurring as the procurement counterpart as engagements expand. LAPAM is the state agency that awards the advertising work the buffer then distributes; where Getz signs, the state's ad machinery is the client.

cast.name: Eran Shayovich
cast.role: Strategic communications chief, Ministry of Foreign Affairs
cast.bio: Named on Piro's Exhibit A as the ministry-side contact, and reported by Israeli press as an architect of the 545 million shekel campaign, a characterization attributed to that reporting. The MFA-side hub where the opinion budget meets its vendors.

cast.name: Oren Marmorstein
cast.bio: Named in TCG's filings as supervising the pipeline's first documented engagement, the February 2025 TCG contract that predates the public campaign. The earliest ministry name in the record.

cast.name: Gideon Sa'ar
cast.bio: Named in Sniper Advertising's 2026 exhibit as a party to the oral agreement, the only minister-level name in any of the eight legs' filings. Being named in a registrant's description of an oral agreement is the filing's characterization; it does not establish personal negotiation.

cast.name: Chad Schnitger
cast.bio: Riverside County political consultant; president of a regional Faith and Freedom Coalition chapter. Contracted through Havas for the church-focused campaign: audience work aimed at American congregations. His sworn expense ledger lists all 742 transaction lines exactly twice, doubling roughly $1.67 million of actual activity into a sworn $3,333,191.86, with zero advertising purchases anywhere in it and $352,949 for a trailer. The discrepancy is documented from his own filing; no charges exist and none are suggested. Walked back his public characterizations twice when contacted by press. Has not responded to comment requests.

cast.name: Uri Steinberg and Yair Levy
cast.bio: Former Israeli Tourism Ministry officials; Steinberg served as tourism commissioner for North America. Their firm took the Esther Project engagement: a $900,000 order of which roughly $700,000 is unaccounted for in the filings, with about twelve weeks of documented pre-registration activity. The tourism-side counterpart to the MFA legs. Silent to all inquiries.

cast.name: Nadav Shtrauchler
cast.bio: Appears in Bridges' pre-registration disbursements with a $15,000 consultant fee. Israeli political strategist with Netanyahu-campaign background, per Israeli press profiles, attributed as such. The strategy layer above the Esther Project's execution.

cast.name: Tzahi Daboush
cast.bio: Former Army Radio military correspondent and communications chief in ministerial offices. Registered the same day as his handshake agreement, the pipeline's fastest paper. The smallest leg by money, and the cleanest by timeline.

cast.name: Yoav Davis
cast.bio: Founder of the Jews of NY platform; Israeli-born, formerly IDF. Registered October 12, 2025 running the L.D.R.S. dual pipe, the pipeline's clearest example of one operator serving parallel principal chains. His filings put the broader L.D.R.S. program's floor above $58 million.

cast.name: Daniel Rosenberg and Tim Piper
cast.bio: A Hollywood producer and a Time 100 advertising director: the prestige leg. Contracted for a $900,000 pilot for the Tourism Ministry, with MFA communications chief Shayovich named on their exhibit. The pipeline's bid for entertainment-grade production values.

cast.name: Frederick T. Hickerson III and Larry Kerschenbaum
cast.bio: Fifty-fifty owners per their registration: Hickerson in Key Largo, Florida; Kerschenbaum a dual US-Israeli citizen living in Israel. Their firm holds the pipeline's only oral agreement with BOTH ministries, Tourism and Foreign Affairs, with Foreign Minister Sa'ar named, on volume-contingent fees: they earn only if the ministries order campaigns. Registered promptly and compliantly. The corporate chain runs through a Wyoming registered-agent nesting that ends at Wyoming Corporate Services, the bulk mail-drop operation NPR profiled. Their website copied GeoDataScience's older site, privacy policy included, per GeoDataScience's own account; the platform their offering resells is GeoDataScience's, whose CEO says no campaigns are running. Their August 4 comment deadline passed without response; a follow-up email is documented.

cast.name: Roger Heaston
cast.role: President and CEO, GeoDataScience Inc. dba Refinition
cast.bio: Signed the Texas assumed-name certificate that connected Refinition to GeoDataScience. On August 1, 2026, became the first company principal in this investigation to respond on the record: confirmed Sniper is a reseller of his platform, said GeoDataScience was unaware of the FARA registration until our inquiry, said no campaigns are running and no foreign-government agreements exist, and stated that any campaign contracted by a reseller 'is executed solely by us,' meaning ministry campaigns ordered through Sniper would run through his firm's hands. Career: NetSuite, Placewise, Supply Strategies. His account is reported as his account; no wrongdoing asserted.

cast.name: GeoDataScience Inc. (dba Refinition)
cast.bio: The platform behind Sniper's offering: same opt-out email, near-identical services copy, and Sniper's privacy policy was Refinition's verbatim. Texas assumed name filed June 4, 2021; California data broker registration #552962 (2022); marketing claims reach into most US adult mobile devices with multi-year location history. Confirmed the reseller relationship August 1, 2026, and says current operations no longer require data broker registration, a position noted as theirs. If the ministries ever order campaigns through Sniper, this is the company that would execute them, by its own description of its architecture.

cast.name: Katherine Reynolds
cast.bio: Signs TCG's filings on the twin $1,545,000 monthly rate and the $9.89 million retroactive order. Identification and role within SKDK/TCG still being verified; listed here because her signature appears on the money.

cast.name: Ryan Patrick Coyne
cast.role: CEO and owner, Olympic Media LLC dba Starboard
cast.bio: Sole owner of the ninth registered leg, per his own registration. Arlington, Virginia; born 1987; company formed through LegalZoom in January 2017. Contracted October 13, 2026 by LDRS Group LLC for a $500,000, 120-day persuasion pilot measured by polling and 'Cost-Per-Converted-Voice,' and swears he will personally handle audience construction, content distribution and measurement. Disclosed a $7,000 contribution to Bernie Moreno for Senate eleven days before signing; lawful with disclosure. Registered fifteen days after the contract. Comment request pending.

cast.name: Udi Mendelovits
cast.bio: Signs the Starboard contract for LDRS Group LLC, One World Trade Center, as the party acting 'on behalf of the State of Israel.' The first named officer of the second pipe to surface in a US filing. The relationship between LDRS Group LLC of New York and L.D.R.S Group LTD of Tel Aviv, named on Davis Media's 2025 short form, is unexamined. Professional record only; no conduct asserted.

updates.text: Site overhauled: filings now sync daily from DOJ's FARA bulk data; a Filings database, per-registrant pages and a live Israel-registrant index were added. Dockets pulled: a ninth leg, Olympic Media LLC dba Starboard (#7788), registered October 28 under LDRS Group LLC 'on behalf of the State of Israel' for a $500,000 persuasion pilot. Clock Tower's October 30 supplemental: $25.5 million received April-September, $18.39 million disbursed, cumulative receipts $40.5 million; an October 5 order extends the $4.5 million monthly rate through December 2026. Piro added $440,000 in two orders. Show Faith received $977,658 more and filed an undoubled ledger. Bridges filed six months of nothing. Everything new is marked DRAFT until verified against the PDFs; comment requests for the new material have not yet been sent.

The original services agreement read in full: production quotas of 100 assets and 5,000 variants per month, monthly SEO via the MarketBrew AI platform, a matching-funds provision, and the deliverable quoted verbatim: deployment of websites and content to deliver GPT framing results on GPT conversations. The December exhibit read: the launch budget restructured to a $9 million pool with monthly influence and network maps added. Corporate identity resolved: a single-member Delaware LLC formed June 11, 2025, confirmed against the state registry. Detailed questions sent to Clock Tower X with a deadline of August 13. New article published: Before You Ask ChatGPT About Israel, in the Articles tab. Prior reporting credited throughout: Poulson, Responsible Statecraft, TIME, Axios.

Major docket and corpus findings. The content mesh enumerated from Clock Tower's own filings: eleven confirmed properties (allyvia, cognitura, alliesforpeace, factsignal, TheTruthAboutIran, justorium, paxpoint, culturavia, innovascope, econora, compassionpulse) plus two candidates under verification; roughly 97% of the mesh's citations point at its own sibling sites, and 25 passages describe sister-site content as our analysis. The $31.5M order's ad campaign entered the record July 18: Strong Allies. Safer America., on Trump and Netanyahu imagery. Sampling across 179 content filings indicates five to seven thousand pages filed in nine months; June 2 batch filings carry internal content dates of April 30 and May 8 against a 48-hour filing statute, while July filings run same-day. Personnel: three new short-forms July 31 including the roster's first web developer; Alexander Miller's termination reported in one day on August 4, against the prior termination's eight-and-a-half-month lag. Sniper's August 4 comment deadline passed without response. New: a Beyond 545 tab documenting Israel's other registered influence campaigns, kept deliberately separate from the Project 545 count.

Clock Tower X docket check: fourth exhibit formally papers the $31.5M April-October order under an agreement dated June 2 (April and May ran first); a July 14 amendment reports an October 2025 staff departure eight and a half months late; two new short-form registrants filed July 9; informational materials continue every two days, about 169 filings since October 2025. And a first: GeoDataScience (dba Refinition), the platform behind Sniper's site, responded on the record, confirming the reseller arrangement and stating it was unaware of the FARA registration until our inquiry. Supplemental link swapped to the official DOJ copy. Articles tab added, collecting the full Feral America series. Full write-up at feralamerica.substack.com.

Expanded comment requests sent to Sniper Advertising Services and to the platform vendor whose legal language appears on its site; response deadlines August 4, 2026. Full archives of both companies' websites captured via the Wayback Machine. Sniper's Wyoming registered-agent chain documented, with the 2011 NPR reporting on Wyoming Corporate Services added to the document library.

All outstanding comment windows closed without response, including Clock Tower X (July 22) and the DOJ FARA Unit (July 24, covering both the questions and the document request for the broken supplemental link). Contact address live: localtip@proton.me. Late responses will be added in full and logged here.
Leg eight added: Sniper Advertising Services (#7745), direct-to-ministries location-capture advertising; Wyoming registry chain documented; comment requested.

Clock Tower supplemental analyzed (via DCNF mirror; DOJ link broken): $15M receipts, Havas loan, personal loan repayment, the Israel-erasure statements, the Carlson/Owens/Kent content ledger, the disclosed congressional contribution.

Show Faith doubled ledger verified computationally: 742 lines, zero non-duplicates, actual spending exactly $1,666,595.93. Referral transmitted to congressional oversight staff. No response from Show Faith by stated deadline.
Legs five through seven documented: Piro, Genesis 21, TCG/SKDK (the true origin, Feb 18, 2025); the Havas both-sides finding; Getz identified as the throughline; twin-rate finding.
Bridges and Davis Media dockets pulled: the twelve-week gap, the $700K hole, the no-role claim, the second pipe.

beyond.n: GlobalPoint International, for Stark Aerospace / IAI
beyond.text: A Virginia firm registered to build the relationship of Israel Aerospace Industries, via its Mississippi subsidiary Stark Aerospace, with "the Trump-Vance Administration, Congress and across the US government," at $45,000 a month plus a $100,000 expense pool, with a named-agency target list including the Missile Defense Agency and a provision for op-eds under "influential third-party voices." The filing's appendix describes IAI as a state owned enterprise of the Government of Israel. Responded on the record August 5, 2026: confirms the engagement, frames its registration as elected "out of an abundance of caution," and declines per firm policy to discuss specifics. New Stark exhibit filed September 18, 2026 (draft: not yet read).

beyond.n: PLUS Communications, for the Ministry of Finance
beyond.text: Published rates and political activity marked yes; investor-relations work around Israel's debt offerings. The audience is bond markets: the campaign to keep the borrowing cheap. Comment deadline August 7, 2026 passed; silence documented.

beyond.n: Weber Shandwick (IPG DXTRA), for the Ministry of Finance
beyond.text: An Interpublic Group agency handling investor relations around Israel's debt offerings, rates sealed, political activity marked no, with an accompanying media buy. The same senior deputy accountant general appears across both Finance files. New supplemental filed September 29, 2026 (draft: not yet read).

beyond.n: Mercury Public Affairs, for the Misgav Institute
beyond.text: A one-month, $5,000 engagement, signed for Mercury by former US Senator David Vitter: distribute a report co-authored by Gilad Erdan, Israel's former Ambassador to the UN, arguing for American disengagement from the United Nations, to the foreign-policy committees, both Appropriations subcommittees, the NSC, State, OMB, and the US Mission to the UN, followed by a three-day Washington fly-in in late July 2026. The filing swears Misgav is an independent think tank. The Misgav principal was terminated July 24, 2026 per DOJ's principal list.

beyond.n: Pearson Unlimited, LLC, for Xtend Reality, Inc.
beyond.text: Coreco 'CJ' Pearson's company registered September 10, 2026 for Xtend Reality, Inc., an Israeli private company, not a government organ. Listed here because DOJ tags the principal's country as Israel; kept out of the Project 545 count. Reported separately in the Feral America video series.
A law firm registration for an Israeli individual, principal added February 23, 2026. Logged for completeness; outside the opinion campaign.

articles.t: Project 545: How Trump's Campaign Manager Ended Up Working for Israel
articles.p: The map of the campaign: a 545 million shekel budget, eight registered foreign agents, five money routes, and the documents that connect them. Start here.

articles.p: The biggest leg: $15 million received, a $31.5 million order ending the month before the midterms, the registration that erased Israel "in error," and a content ledger aimed at American commentators.
The geofencing contract aimed at American churches, and the sworn expense ledger that lists every transaction exactly twice, doubling a $1.67 million campaign into a $3.33 million one under oath.

articles.p: The defense track, the credit desk, and the watchtower that catches nothing: three more channels from one evening in the database, deliberately fenced from the Project 545 count.

articles.t: Before You Ask ChatGPT About Israel
articles.p: Eleven fake research institutes, a 97 percent self-citation rate, production quotas in the contract, and the deliverable in Clock Tower's own filing: GPT framing results on GPT conversations. The flagship investigation of the content network.
